title: Ingress posture case
description: The ingress posture case, as defined in The Software Field Guide, issue #82: the secure-developer-ingress chapter's YAML — the platform's edge posture as data. The case declares the DNS containment boundary (the zone every wildcard must stay inside), the request policy (default-deny and the decision that backs it), the allowed domain patterns (concrete hosts and contained wildcards, each with its intent in words), the TLS certificates with their rotation clocks, the service level objectives with the pagers behind them, the route classes the edge carries next to the classes the audit logs, and the kill path the platform swears it can pull. This schema mirrors the shape rules of the Rego validator (policies/ingress); the validator additionally enforces the semantic rules a JSON schema cannot — wildcards contained inside the zone, certificate windows valid and unexpired against the injected clock, every declared route class logged, no duplicated coverage, and the kill path rehearsed against the drill record.

version.description: Version of the case. Posture is versioned like code — a posture case nobody re-reads is a posture case nobody still believes.

reviewedOn.description: Date the case was last reviewed, YYYY-MM-DD. The validator flags reviews older than 365 days and dates in the future.

owner.description: The team that owns the edge. A posture case with an owner and a review cadence is the discipline.

zone.description: The DNS containment boundary, e.g. dev.internal. Every wildcard the case declares is held inside this zone; a wildcard the zone cannot hold is an admit-all in disguise.

requestPolicy.description: The edge's request policy. Deny by default, admit by exception — the allow list stays an allow list only while the default is deny.

defaultDeny.description: Whether the edge rejects every request the allowed domains do not admit. False is not permissive honesty, it is a finding.

decision.description: The decision the edge makes by default, in words — the sentence a reviewer reads back.

domains.description: The allowed domain patterns — the allow list. Concrete hosts and contained wildcards only; the validator flags a pattern broader than the zone can hold.

pattern.description: The admitted host pattern. A concrete host (no wildcard) is the narrowest admit; a leading '*.suffix' wildcard is held when the suffix names at least two labels inside the zone.

intent.description: Why this pattern is admitted, in words. An allow list row without its intent is a row nobody can review.

certs.description: The TLS certificates the edge serves, each with its rotation clock. The validator flags a cert expired against the injected clock and warns for one inside its rotation window — the cert that rotates late is the cert that expires.

serves.description: The host this certificate serves. Findings cite it verbatim.

notBefore.description: The first day the certificate is valid, YYYY-MM-DD.

notAfter.description: The last day the certificate is valid, YYYY-MM-DD. Must not precede notBefore; must lie in the future against the injected clock.

rotateByDays.description: The rotation clock in days: the cert must be replaced this many days before it expires. The rotation window is what turns an expiry into a routine, not an incident.

slos.description: The service level objectives the platform declares for the edge — each with the pager that answers when it breaks. An SLO nobody pages is a promise nobody keeps.

name.description: The SLO's name, e.g. edge availability. Findings and cards cite it verbatim.

target.description: What the platform promises, in words, e.g. 99.9% of requests served inside 200ms.

pager.description: Who or what answers when the target breaks — the on-call, the escalation path, the automation. A target without a pager is a hope.

routes.description: The route classes the edge carries. Classes must be unique — duplicated coverage is double-counted coverage — and every declared class must appear in loggedRouteClasses.

class.description: The route class, e.g. developer-app, partner-api, health-check.

loggedRouteClasses.description: The route classes the audit logs. Traffic the edge carries but the audit never sees is the gap this validator exists to find.

killPath.description: The kill path — the lever the platform swears it can pull. Declared here, rehearsed on the drill record; a kill path never rehearsed is a promise the platform has never kept.

name.description: The kill path's name, e.g. seal-edge. The drill record rehearses it by this name.

effect.description: What pulling the lever does, in words — the effect a reviewer reads before an incident reads it for them.
